about.intro_content: Prof. Jun Ma is an Academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Deputy President of Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC) in Guangzhou, China. He is a Professor of Radiation Oncology and Director of the Key Laboratory of Multidisciplinary Diagnosis and Treatment of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma (NPC).
about.detailed_content: Prof. Ma's research has focused on prognosis prediction, TNM staging refinement, and comprehensive treatment strategies for nasopharyngeal carcinoma across a career spanning more than three decades. As corresponding author, he has published over 50 papers in journals including the New England Journal of Medicine, The Lancet, JAMA, The BMJ and Nature Medicine, and has led multiple phase 3 clinical trials that now inform international NPC treatment guidelines. He trained at Hunan Medical University and Sun Yat-sen University of Medical Sciences before completing a postdoctoral fellowship in Radiation Oncology at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center.

why_cards.title: Academician, Chinese Academy of Sciences

why_cards.title: Practice-Changing Clinical Trials

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Jun Ma

items.question: Does Prof. Jun Ma accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What cancers does Prof. Jun Ma specialise in?
items.answer: Prof. Ma's clinical and research focus is nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), including locoregionally advanced, recurrent, and metastatic disease, with additional contributions to head and neck cancer treatment guidelines.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Jun Ma involved in clinical trials for nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Ma has led numerous phase 3 clinical trials in NPC, including studies combining immunotherapy with chemoradiotherapy, and continues to serve as an investigator on active trials at SYSUCC.

items.question: Why is Prof. Jun Ma considered a leading authority on nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
items.answer: Prof. Ma is an Academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences whose research has helped refine NPC staging systems and shape international treatment guidelines, with corresponding-author publications in journals including NEJM, The Lancet, and JAMA.
